We've completed the Polaris RFI spreadsheet and attached three items that should address Section B: a network diagram that shows control-plane separation, an operator separation runbook excerpt, and our maintenance-window matrix. Highlights below; the attachments include more evidence and screenshots where helpful.

High-level answers (summary):
- Operator separation: Redwood Private supports a distinct operator control plane that terminates on a customer-managed jump-hosts/VPN only. Operator admin traffic uses a dedicated management VPC or self-hosted bastion; operator accounts are not present on customer-facing hosts. Role-based access is enforced with short-lived certificates and MFA.
- Outbound egress: By default an air-gapped deployment has zero egress. Where outbound signing or telemetry is required, we provide a push-only package signing workflow initiated from an on-prem artifact repository; outbound connections must be explicitly enabled by the customer and are limited to allowlists and signed cert pinning.
- Maintenance & patching: We provide an operator runbook for offline patch application and upgrade bundles (signed), plus an operator-assisted staging process and pre-signed delta packages so upgrades do not require inbound connections. The runbook includes steps for human-in-the-loop verification and audit logging of all operator actions.

Rishi / Mina — draft below for Polaris; please edit if you'd like. I'll attach the signed-sample manifest and a brief excerpt from the runbook.

Addendum (draft):
- Bundle signing: We generate upgrade bundles as tar.gz archives. Each archive is signed using an RSA-4096 key stored in a customer-managed HSM (recommended) or Redwood-managed KMS per contract. Signatures use PKCS#1 v1.5 with SHA-256. Verification is performed on the target host using a short Go utility (redwood-verify) which only accepts a pre-provisioned public key fingerprint. The signed manifest (manifest.json + signature.asc) is included alongside the artifact.
- Offline verification workflow: Operator copies the signed bundle to an air-gapped staging host via removable media or a customer-approved transfer method. On the staging host, redwood-verify validates the manifest and checks the bundle checksum before extraction. No external network calls are made.
- Audit log handling: Operator actions are recorded locally in structured JSON logs. We support log-forwarding to a customer SIEM agent via a push-only mechanism (customer-configured forwarder), which transmits logs directly to the customer's collector (no relay through Redwood). We can also provide signed attestations of action timestamps on request.

Attachments to include: signed-manifest-example.tar.gz (sample), runbook-excerpt-ops.md (excerpt)

Laura Bennett
Director, Product Security, Redwood Inference
